outcome: Claimed false on 9 Sep 2026: Lai, Lim and Ren (arXiv:2609.10420) give a continuous, piecewise-quadratic function on R^30 that they say has no finite lattice expression in polynomials, found with a multi-agent, multi-model AI setup; the claim is an unrefereed preprint with no named expert response found in the five weeks since posting, and a 2025 preprint by Lai and Lim proves the conjecture only for splines on hyperplane partitions.
problem_asks: (1) For every dimension n, every piecewise-polynomial function f: R^n -> R (a finite cover of R^n by closed semialgebraic pieces, on each of which f agrees with a polynomial) can be written as f = sup_i inf_j g_ij with finitely many polynomials g_ij in R[x_1,...,x_n]. The statement quantifies over all n, so a failure in one dimension refutes it as written. (2) Sub-cases the sources name as settled: n = 1 and n = 2 (Mahe, 1984; Efroymson also reported for n = 2, unverified). (3) Sources name n >= 3 as open in general (Wikipedia, revision of 16 Feb 2026; Lai-Lim 2025 introduction). (4) Wording to note: the Wikipedia statement says 'piecewise-polynomial function'; the 2025 and 2026 papers say 'continuous piecewise polynomial' and 'semialgebraic spline'. Sup and inf of polynomials are continuous, so the question concerns continuous functions. (5) Madden (1989) gives an equivalent local formulation, at pairs of points of the real spectrum and their separating ideals. That equivalence is not asked by the bullet, but it is the framework most of the partial results use.

events.what_happened: L. Mahe, 'On the Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture', Rocky Mountain J. Math. 14 (1984), 983-985 (DOI 10.1216/RMJ-1984-14-4-983), proves the conjecture for n = 2. Wikipedia credits Mahe with n = 1 and n = 2, citing Atlas Conferences (1999). I did not open the note: the Project Euclid page returned empty, so the n = 2 statement and the bibliographic record come from the Wikipedia article and search snippets.
events.delivers: Pierce-Birkhoff for n = 2 (and n = 1, per Wikipedia): every piecewise-polynomial function on R^2 is a sup of infs of finitely many polynomials. Restricted to two variables.

events.what_happened: F. Lucas, D. Schaub, M. Spivakovsky, 'On the Pierce-Birkhoff Conjecture', arXiv 1207.6463 (single version, submitted 27 Jul 2012). Per the arXiv abstract page (opened): introduces a complexity for pairs of points and a 'Strong Connectedness' conjecture; proves it in dimension 2, which gives the Connectedness and Pierce-Birkhoff conjectures in any dimension under a height condition (the abstract says 'less than 2'; the 2018 paper says at most 2); and proves Connectedness, hence Pierce-Birkhoff, when dim A = ht = 3, the pair has complexity 1, and A is excellent with residue field R. A journal version may exist (a search link points to AFST 21, 2012); I did not confirm it.
events.delivers: Pierce-Birkhoff for the local pair statements under a height bound, in any dimension (per the abstract), and for the ring class dim A = ht = 3 with complexity 1, excellent, residue field R. These are restricted classes of rings, not all of R^n for n = 3.
events.remains: Pierce-Birkhoff for n = 3 in general, and for n >= 4 in general.
events.doubts: The height condition is stated as 'less than 2' in the abstract I read and as 'at most 2' in the 2018 paper. The journal version, if any, is unverified.
events.direction: Partial progress toward the conjecture in restricted cases. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: F. Lucas, D. Schaub, M. Spivakovsky, 'On the strong separation conjecture', arXiv 1802.09389 (arXiv identifier gives February 2018). Described in search snippets (the arXiv page and the Angers copy were not opened): proves the Strong Separation Conjecture, the r = 1 case of the Strong Connectedness conjecture, for points alpha, beta in 'good position' relative to a fixed polynomial f in R[x,z]. The same snippets say a version of it in dimension n-1 implies connectedness in dimension n when the height is at most n-1.
events.delivers: Reported: a separation statement for pairs in good position relative to one polynomial in two variables (the ring R[x,z]). Two variables is the case already settled, so this is not a Pierce-Birkhoff result for n >= 3.
events.remains: Pairs not in good position; all of n >= 3.
events.doubts: Described from search snippets only. I did not open the paper.
events.direction: Partial progress toward the separation conjecture. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Z. Lai, L. Lim, 'Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture is true for splines', arXiv 2507.07976 (v1 10 Jul 2025; v2 16 Jul 2025, 'slight improvement to Lemma 4.1 (reduced p + 1 to p)'). Per the arXiv abstract and HTML (opened): proves that every spline, meaning a continuous piecewise polynomial of degree d on a hyperplane partition of R^n, is max-definable (a finite max-min of polynomials), for all d and n. Gives a purely existential proof, then effective bounds (degree 2d+1 and chamber count O(b^(2n^2) d^n) per the fetched text). The introduction says: 'Aside from the case d=1 and the case n<=2, the Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture is not known to hold for any other values of d and n.'
events.revisions: v1 10 Jul 2025; v2 16 Jul 2025 (arXiv abstract page).
events.delivers: Pierce-Birkhoff for splines on hyperplane partitions, for all d and n, with the restriction that the pieces are defined by linear polynomials. The paper states that the conjecture 'holds for any hyperplane partition'. General semialgebraic partitions are not covered.
events.remains: Pierce-Birkhoff for continuous piecewise polynomials whose pieces are not hyperplane-defined, in every n >= 3 (the general case).
events.doubts: (a) The main theorem is stated for the class 'max-definable' (generated from polynomials and constants by addition, multiplication, maximization and scalar multiplication, Definition 2.4 per the fetched text). Conjecture 1.1 asks for a max-min formula. I could not confirm from the text I read that the paper derives the max-min form from max-definability, so whether the theorem is exactly the conjecture's form is unresolved. (b) No conflict with the 2026 counterexample was found: the 2026 paper says the spline result 'does not extend to arbitrary semialgebraic partitions, even for piecewise quadratic functions', which matches this paper's scope.
events.direction: Affirmative, for the restricted class of splines on hyperplane partitions.

events.what_happened: Z. Lai, L. Lim, J. Ren, 'Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture is false', arXiv 2609.10420 (math.AG; MSC 14P10, 26B40, 13J25, 41A15, 52C35, 52B55; '7 pages, 1 figure'; v1 submitted 9 Sep 2026, 16:37 UTC; no later version found, since the v2 abstract URL returned HTTP 404 when checked on 13 Oct 2026). Abstract (per the arXiv HTML fetch): 'We provide a counterexample to the Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture: a continuous function that is piecewise quadratic on a finite collection of semialgebraic sets that partition R^n but that cannot be expressed as a finite lattice combination of polynomials.' Per the authors' TeX (fetched): the function lives on the 30-dimensional space of pairs (X,Y) of real symmetric 5x5 matrices; Theorem: 'The function f is a continuous, positively homogeneous of degree two, and piecewise quadratic polynomial', and 'It admits no finite lattice expression in real polynomials of arbitrary degrees.' The same paper says counterexamples for n = 5, 6, 7, 30 and 72 'have also been verified through Lean-formalization' (link to GitHub repository), and that 'our setup has also generated counterexamples of dimensions n = 5, 6, 7, 22, 24, 72 although they are harder for a human reader to verify'. The paper describes its n = 30 example as 'chosen because it can be readily checked by hand'.
events.revisions: v1 only, 9 Sep 2026 (arXiv abstract page). arxiv.org/abs/2609.10420v2 returned HTTP 404 on 13 Oct 2026. The arXiv PDF could not be read by my tools.
events.delivers: As the authors state it: a continuous function on R^30 (and, per the paper's Lean claims, on R^5, R^6, R^7 and R^72) that is piecewise quadratic on a finite semialgebraic partition and admits no finite lattice expression in polynomials of arbitrary degree. The paper defines 'lattice expression' as generated by addition, multiplication and maximization of polynomial functions. That class contains all max-min forms, so non-membership in it rules out a max-min representation. If the paper's theorem is correct, the conjecture as stated fails in those dimensions. The paper also says its setup generated n = 22 and n = 24 counterexamples, but describes neither.
events.remains: Whether the non-representability argument is correct is unverified by me. The conjecture quantifies over all n, so one failing dimension refutes the statement as written. Dimensions n = 3 and n = 4 are not addressed in the arXiv text. The repository's n = 4 claim is a separate event. Dimensions 1 and 2 are not in dispute.

events.directly_checkable: The n = 30 object: f on pairs (X,Y) of real symmetric 5x5 matrices, with P = XY, h = the minimum of 40 quadratic forms P_ii +/- 4P_ij (per the fetched rendering of Section 1), f = h where h > 0 and det X > 0, and f = 0 elsewhere. By hand: positivity of the forms gives |P_ij| < P_ii/4 for each off-diagonal entry in a row (four per row), so each row of P is strictly dominant, hence P, X and Y are invertible; this is what the paper's Lemma 2 needs and is consistent with the stated continuity and degree-2 homogeneity. I did not check the non-representability claim, which is the substance of the result.
events.doubts: (1) No named external reader, referee report, blog post or public response was found in 37 searches. (2) The README says the main proof 'has undergone careful human expert checking' and names no one. (3) The dimension lists disagree: the paper gives Lean-verified n = 5, 6, 7, 30, 72 and generated n = 22, 24; the repository has folders for n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 30, 72 and none for 22 or 24. The n = 4 and n = 8 constructions appear only in the README. (4) Human review status in the README is 'pending' for n = 4, 'ongoing' for n = 5, 6, 7, and none claimed for n = 8, while the paper presents n = 5, 6, 7 as Lean-verified. (5) The key steps are attributed to AI systems by the authors (see ai), and the non-representability argument was, per the authors, partly produced by GPT investigations. (6) The definition of 'lattice expression' is stated with +, x and max, while the conjecture asks for max-min. This does not weaken a refutation (see delivers), but readers should check the definition against the PDF, which I could not read.
events.direction: Against the conjecture as stated: it asserts that a piecewise-polynomial function on R^30 (and in the other dimensions the paper names) is a finite max-min of polynomials, and the paper says this is false.
events.object: A continuous, positively homogeneous of degree 2, piecewise quadratic function f: R^30 -> R, identified with pairs (X,Y) of real symmetric 5x5 matrices with P = XY. h is the minimum of 40 quadratic forms P_ii +/- 4P_ij (ordered pairs i != j, by my count of the 40); f = h where h > 0 and det X > 0; f = 0 elsewhere. The object is explicit. The claim that it has no finite lattice expression in polynomials of arbitrary degree is a proved negative statement from the authors, not an existence proof, and I did not check it. The paper gives Lean-verified counterparts for n = 5, 6, 7 and 72, which the repository folders list.

summary: The conjecture was open for n >= 3 in every source I read up to July 2025: Wikipedia (revision of 16 Feb 2026, opened) lists only n = 1 and n = 2 as proved (Mahe, 1984), and the 2025 spline paper's introduction says the conjecture is 'not known to hold for any other values of d and n' beyond d = 1 and n <= 2. Within the window, two things happened. First, Lai and Lim (arXiv 2507.07976, 10 Jul 2025, opened) proved the conjecture for splines on hyperplane partitions for all d and n, with effective bounds. Second, Lai, Lim and Ren (arXiv 2609.10420, submitted 9 Sep 2026, opened via the abstract, the arXiv HTML and the authors' TeX source fetched through a summarising tool) claim a counterexample, which the authors say was found with the assistance of 'our multi-agent, multi-model setup that chains together GPT 5.6, GPT 6, Claude Opus 5, and Claude Fable 5.1'. The object is explicit: a function on R^30 built from pairs of symmetric 5x5 matrices (X,Y) with P = XY, h = min of 40 forms P_ii +/- 4P_ij, f = h where h > 0 and det X > 0, and 0 otherwise. The paper says f is continuous, positively homogeneous of degree 2 and piecewise quadratic, and admits no finite lattice expression in polynomials of arbitrary degree. I checked the elementary parts by hand and they hold together: positivity of the forms gives |P_ij| < P_ii/4 for each off-diagonal entry, so P, X and Y are invertible, which the continuity of f requires. I did not check the non-representability argument, which is the whole content of the claim, and I could not read the PDF with my tools (the PDF was saved to a location outside the project directory, and I did not open it). Engagement: 37 searches, including the title, the authors' names, the Lean, formal-conjectures, MathOverflow, blog and social-media angles, found no referee report, expert blog, Quanta or Tao coverage, Lean Zulip thread, or formal-conjectures entry for the preprint. The only later material is the authors' own repository. That repository's README says the main proof 'has undergone careful human expert checking and is formalized in Lean' without naming anyone, while the same README gives human review as 'pending' for n = 4, 'ongoing' for n = 5, 6, 7, and none claimed for n = 8. The paper and repository disagree on the dimension list: the paper names n = 5, 6, 7, 30, 72 as Lean-verified and n = 22, 24 as generated but harder to check, and the repository contains folders for n = 4 and 8 and none for 22 or 24. Whether the 4- and 8-dimensional claims exist in the paper is therefore a live question; the arXiv text does not mention them. Close calls: (a) Whether the 2026 result is a refutation depends wholly on the non-representability proof, which I could not read. Readers should weigh the elementary checks as strong evidence about the construction and no evidence about the key step. (b) Scope: the paper defines 'lattice expression' with addition, multiplication and maximization, which is broader than the max-min form in the conjecture. Non-membership in the broader class still rules out a max-min representation, so the refutation does not depend on this, but the 2025 spline theorem is stated for the broader class ('max-definable'), and I could not confirm from the text I read that it implies the max-min form the conjecture asks for. (c) The AI attribution is strong and specific in the authors' own words. The authors credit GPT investigations with the dimension-72 construction and the exclusion argument (per the arXiv HTML rendering), and ChatGPT with the dimension-30 symmetric-matrix construction ('With further assistance from ChatGPT, we obtained the symmetric-matrix construction in dimension~30', per the TeX). The human role is described as 'high-level guidance on the mathematical significance of the different research targets'. The paper also states that the spline result from 2025 was 'a purely human endeavor with no AI usage', and the 2025 paper itself has no AI statement. Other AI-related results surfaced by the searches (Jacobian conjecture, Borsuk problem in dimension 63, Erdos unit distance) concern other problems and are not recorded here. The quoted sentences came through a summarising fetch tool, so the exact wording should be checked against the PDF or the TeX before relying on it.
competing_reading: Read the 2026 result as not yet a refutation. It is a single unrefereed preprint, its key step (non-representability) was not readable by me and is not summarised anywhere I could read, no named expert has responded in five weeks, the README contradicts itself on human review, and the dimension lists in the paper and the repository do not match. Against that, the authors give explicit data, an explicit Lean-verification claim for five dimensions, and an explicit statement that the n = 30 example was chosen because it can be checked by hand. The elementary parts I checked are consistent with the construction. On this reading the claim is credible enough to test but not yet established.
what_would_settle_it: A named mathematician in real algebraic geometry, or a referee report, that checks the non-representability argument for the n = 30 example. Failing that, an inspection of the Lean files in the n = 30 folder: that the theorem statement matches the paper's definitions of 'lattice expression' and 'piecewise quadratic', that it contains no sorry, and that it builds in the stated Lean and Mathlib version. Also a resolution of the dimension-list discrepancy and of the README's human-review statements, and any published version or v2 of arXiv:2609.10420. For the 2025 spline result, a check that its max-definable class is equivalent to the max-min form the conjecture asks for.

event.what_happened: Z. Lai, L. Lim, J. Ren, 'Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture is false', arXiv 2609.10420 (math.AG; MSC 14P10, 26B40, 13J25, 41A15, 52C35, 52B55; '7 pages, 1 figure'; v1 submitted 9 Sep 2026, 16:37 UTC; no later version found, since the v2 abstract URL returned HTTP 404 when checked on 13 Oct 2026). Abstract (per the arXiv HTML fetch): 'We provide a counterexample to the Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture: a continuous function that is piecewise quadratic on a finite collection of semialgebraic sets that partition R^n but that cannot be expressed as a finite lattice combination of polynomials.' Per the authors' TeX (fetched): the function lives on the 30-dimensional space of pairs (X,Y) of real symmetric 5x5 matrices; Theorem: 'The function f is a continuous, positively homogeneous of degree two, and piecewise quadratic polynomial', and 'It admits no finite lattice expression in real polynomials of arbitrary degrees.' The same paper says counterexamples for n = 5, 6, 7, 30 and 72 'have also been verified through Lean-formalization' (link to GitHub repository), and that 'our setup has also generated counterexamples of dimensions n = 5, 6, 7, 22, 24, 72 although they are harder for a human reader to verify'. The paper describes its n = 30 example as 'chosen because it can be readily checked by hand'.
event.revisions: v1 only, 9 Sep 2026 (arXiv abstract page). arxiv.org/abs/2609.10420v2 returned HTTP 404 on 13 Oct 2026. The arXiv PDF could not be read by my tools.
event.delivers: As the authors state it: a continuous function on R^30 (and, per the paper's Lean claims, on R^5, R^6, R^7 and R^72) that is piecewise quadratic on a finite semialgebraic partition and admits no finite lattice expression in polynomials of arbitrary degree. The paper defines 'lattice expression' as generated by addition, multiplication and maximization of polynomial functions. That class contains all max-min forms, so non-membership in it rules out a max-min representation. If the paper's theorem is correct, the conjecture as stated fails in those dimensions. The paper also says its setup generated n = 22 and n = 24 counterexamples, but describes neither.
event.remains: Whether the non-representability argument is correct is unverified by me. The conjecture quantifies over all n, so one failing dimension refutes the statement as written. Dimensions n = 3 and n = 4 are not addressed in the arXiv text. The repository's n = 4 claim is a separate event. Dimensions 1 and 2 are not in dispute.

event.directly_checkable: The n = 30 object: f on pairs (X,Y) of real symmetric 5x5 matrices, with P = XY, h = the minimum of 40 quadratic forms P_ii +/- 4P_ij (per the fetched rendering of Section 1), f = h where h > 0 and det X > 0, and f = 0 elsewhere. By hand: positivity of the forms gives |P_ij| < P_ii/4 for each off-diagonal entry in a row (four per row), so each row of P is strictly dominant, hence P, X and Y are invertible; this is what the paper's Lemma 2 needs and is consistent with the stated continuity and degree-2 homogeneity. I did not check the non-representability claim, which is the substance of the result.
event.doubts: (1) No named external reader, referee report, blog post or public response was found in 37 searches. (2) The README says the main proof 'has undergone careful human expert checking' and names no one. (3) The dimension lists disagree: the paper gives Lean-verified n = 5, 6, 7, 30, 72 and generated n = 22, 24; the repository has folders for n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 30, 72 and none for 22 or 24. The n = 4 and n = 8 constructions appear only in the README. (4) Human review status in the README is 'pending' for n = 4, 'ongoing' for n = 5, 6, 7, and none claimed for n = 8, while the paper presents n = 5, 6, 7 as Lean-verified. (5) The key steps are attributed to AI systems by the authors (see ai), and the non-representability argument was, per the authors, partly produced by GPT investigations. (6) The definition of 'lattice expression' is stated with +, x and max, while the conjecture asks for max-min. This does not weaken a refutation (see delivers), but readers should check the definition against the PDF, which I could not read.
event.direction: Against the conjecture as stated: it asserts that a piecewise-polynomial function on R^30 (and in the other dimensions the paper names) is a finite max-min of polynomials, and the paper says this is false.
event.object: A continuous, positively homogeneous of degree 2, piecewise quadratic function f: R^30 -> R, identified with pairs (X,Y) of real symmetric 5x5 matrices with P = XY. h is the minimum of 40 quadratic forms P_ii +/- 4P_ij (ordered pairs i != j, by my count of the 40); f = h where h > 0 and det X > 0; f = 0 elsewhere. The object is explicit. The claim that it has no finite lattice expression in polynomials of arbitrary degree is a proved negative statement from the authors, not an existence proof, and I did not check it. The paper gives Lean-verified counterparts for n = 5, 6, 7 and 72, which the repository folders list.

judgement.why: The statement quantifies over every n, so an explicit counterexample on R^30 refutes it as written: whole scope, but unreviewed (unnamed README checking and an unopened Lean build are not digestion) and doubtful given internal inconsistencies, though not not_credible given the authors and explicit, partly hand-checked object. AI role is generated: the authors credit GPT investigations with the exclusion argument and ChatGPT with the dimension-30 construction, with humans giving high-level guidance; the Claude models and the Codex/Claude Code harnesses get no specific output in their quotes, so they are not credited. The repository's n = 4 and n = 8 constructions only lower the smallest counterexample dimension of an already-refuted statement, so bound. Lai–Lim 2025 settles a class of objects (hyperplane-partition splines): case. Wagner and LSS 2012 prove the conjecture for other rings or restricted local settings, treated as variant; reductions and frameworks are none; Mahe 2007 is none since its content is unknown.
judgement.doubts: Mahe 2007 may contain a genuine partial n = 3 result (could be case) but the record cannot say. The 2025 spline theorem is stated for 'max-definable' functions; whether that equals the max-min form was not confirmed. All 2026 quotes came via summarising fetches, not the PDF.
